reason: Ryan's theorem holds in principle for stationary axisymmetric vacuum spacetimes. A no-hair test via EMRIs is not structural in both fields, so strength 3 is inflated.

fix.summary: A compact object spiralling into a massive black hole completes ~10⁴–10⁵ orbits in LISA's band. Ryan's theorem says that, for stationary axisymmetric vacuum spacetimes, the phase evolution encodes the mass and current multipoles. Checking Kerr's relation M_ℓ+iS_ℓ=M(ia)^ℓ tests the no-hair theorem with projected precision far beyond electromagnetic probes.

reason: Jacobson's derivation is influential but not taught as core in both nodes. Λ also enters only as an undetermined integration constant.

fix.summary: Jacobson (1995) derived the Einstein equations by requiring the Clausius relation δQ = T dS on every local Rindler horizon. He used the Unruh temperature, an entropy proportional to area and the Raychaudhuri equation; Λ appears only as an integration constant. The result motivates emergent and entropic-gravity proposals in which the field equations are thermodynamic rather than fundamental.

reason: A record with a breaks clause cannot be an identity. The trace anomaly contributes to backreaction rather than solely driving it.

fix.summary: QFT in curved spacetime feeds back into geometry through the semiclassical Einstein equation, whose source is the renormalized expectation value of the stress tensor. Renormalizing ⟨T⟩ produces the conformal trace anomaly, which fixes the flux in 2D evaporation models (CGHS/RST) and drives Starobinsky's anomaly-induced inflation.

reason: The low-energy limit is GR coupled to a dilaton and B-field, not pure GR. The record is one-sided from the GR side, so strength 2.

fix.summary: The closed string's massless spectrum contains a spin-2 graviton. Requiring the worldsheet sigma model on a curved background to stay conformally invariant (vanishing beta functions) imposes Einstein's equations coupled to the dilaton and B-field, plus α′ corrections. GR plus these fields is therefore the low-energy limit of string theory.

reason: Curvature is what no coordinate transformation can remove, not just a Lorentz transformation. The metric is Minkowskian with corrections at second order.

fix.summary: By the equivalence principle, every freely falling frame is locally Minkowskian. GR replaces the global η_{μν} of special relativity by a curved g_{μν} whose tangent space at each point carries the Lorentz group. In Riemann normal coordinates g=η with first derivatives vanishing, so SR laws hold locally. Curvature, the second-order deviation, is what no coordinate choice can remove.

reason: Inflationary seeds come from Bunch–Davies vacuum fluctuations of amplitude H/2π, not literally from fluctuations of the horizon temperature.

fix.summary: The exact de Sitter and FLRW solutions are the standard backgrounds of QFT in curved spacetime. They host Parker's cosmological particle creation, the Bunch–Davies vacuum and the Gibbons–Hawking temperature of the de Sitter horizon. Bunch–Davies fluctuations of light fields, with amplitude H/2π (the same scale as T_GH), seed inflationary perturbations.

reason: A massive graviton has five polarizations; six is the general metric-theory count (Eardley et al. 1973). Parametrized waveform tests are research-level, so strength 2.

fix.summary: GR predicts two tensor polarizations and emission that starts at quadrupole order. Scalar–tensor theories add a breathing mode and dipole radiation from binaries with unequal sensitivities, entering at −1PN. Massive gravity adds dispersion and five polarizations, and generic metric theories allow up to six. Waveform models capture these effects as PN-coefficient deviations or ppE terms.

reason: The physics is correct, but a single measurement pruning one theory class is a substantial specific link, not structural in both fields.
Local Lorentz invariance is one component of the EEP, not identical to it. Schiff's conjecture is unproven in general.

fix.summary: The Einstein equivalence principle combines the weak equivalence principle, local Lorentz invariance and local position invariance. Schiff's conjecture, verified in the THεμ framework but unproven in general, links them. Michelson–Morley-type and clock-comparison tests therefore probe the same principle as Eötvös and redshift tests, and are analysed jointly in Will's THεμ/PPN framework and the gravity-sector SME.

reason: "Generically predict" contradicts the record's own breaks. Only some discrete or emergent models predict linear dispersion.

fix.summary: Some discrete or emergent spacetime models (for example early LQG semiclassical states and lattice-like discreteness) predict Planck-suppressed modified photon dispersion. Fermi GRB timing pushes the linear-order scale past E_Pl, disfavouring such models. Causal sets evade the bound because Poisson sprinkling is statistically Lorentz invariant, and deformed rather than broken symmetry is another way out.

reason: Hyperbolic motion and Rindler horizons are explicitly in the relativistic-kinematics node's scope.
The photon-only formula gives about 2×10¹⁴ g at t₀. The 5×10¹⁴ g figure includes all emitted species (MacGibbon).

fix.map: t_{\rm evap}\approx\frac{5120\pi G^2M^3}{\hbar c^4}\ (\text{photons only})\ \to\ M(t_{\rm evap}=t_0)\approx5\times10^{14}\ \text{g with all emitted species}

reason: Continuous-wave searches constrain under assumptions rather than exclude. Spin bounds cover about 10⁻¹³–2×10⁻¹¹ eV (stellar) and 10⁻¹⁹–10⁻¹⁷ eV (supermassive). Strength 3 is inflated.

fix.summary: A boson whose Compton wavelength is comparable to a Kerr hole's gravitational radius forms hydrogen-like bound states that grow by superradiance while ω < mΩ_H, spinning the hole down. Measured spins of stellar-mass and supermassive black holes disfavour roughly 10⁻¹³–10⁻¹¹ eV and 10⁻¹⁹–10⁻¹⁷ eV, and continuous-GW searches add model-dependent constraints.

reason: The QCD condensate gives about 10⁴⁴ and the Planck cutoff about 10¹²⁰. The range is roughly 40–120 orders, not 50–120.

fix.summary: Lorentz invariance forces vacuum energy to enter the Einstein equations as ρ_vac g_μν, so QFT zero-point energy, the Higgs potential and the QCD condensate all contribute to Λ. Estimates exceed the observed (2.2 meV)⁴ by about 40 (QCD) to 120 (Planck cutoff) orders of magnitude.

reason: An analogy needs a real breaks clause. The gravity side is not taught as Yang–Mills in both fields, so strength 3 is inflated.

fix.summary: Gauging local Lorentz (Poincaré) invariance (Utiyama 1956, Kibble 1961) gives the spin connection as gauge potential and the curvature 2-form as its field strength. GR in tetrad form thus shares the fibre-bundle structure of Yang–Mills, and gauging the full Poincaré group yields Einstein–Cartan theory.
fix.breaks: The Einstein–Hilbert action is linear in curvature, not a Yang–Mills F² action. The tetrad (soldering form) has no Yang–Mills counterpart, and diffeomorphisms are not internal gauge symmetries.

reason: Higgs inflation and Starobinsky gravity coincide only at leading order in large ξ and N. This is not an identity, and the unitarity cutoff is disputed.

fix.summary: A large non-minimal coupling ξh²R (ξ~10⁴) makes the SM Higgs the inflaton. Transforming to the Einstein frame flattens the potential into the same plateau as Starobinsky R+R² gravity, giving n_s≈0.965 and r≈0.003 at N≈60.
fix.breaks: The predictions coincide only at leading order; reheating differs. Burgess, Lee and Trott and Barbón and Espinosa argue that the unitarity cutoff M_P/ξ undermines the model's predictivity.

reason: NRGR integrates out potential modes; radiation gravitons remain and couple to multipoles. Strength 3 is inflated for a one-directional method transfer.

fix.summary: Non-relativistic GR (Goldberger–Rothstein 2006) treats compact bodies as point particles on worldlines, with finite-size operators such as tidal Love numbers. It integrates out potential gravitons with Feynman diagrams and dimensional regularization, leaving radiation gravitons coupled to multipoles. This is the NRQCD-style EFT toolkit applied to post-Newtonian inspirals.

reason: The physics is accurate, but this is a current-research method transfer, not structural in both fields.
The name is about axion domain walls, but the summary lists strings and phase transitions; C1975 covers strings. The link is speculative and one-sided.

fix.summary: Annihilating domain walls of axion-like particles (with a bias term) whose walls decay near 10–100 MeV temperatures produce a stochastic GW background peaking in the nanohertz band. NANOGrav 2023 found such models fit the PTA spectrum comparably to supermassive-binary models.

reason: The SM electroweak transition is a crossover, so the record needs BSM physics. The peak formula omits the O(1) f*/β factor. Strength 3 is inflated.

fix.summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition, which requires physics beyond the SM since the SM transition is a crossover. Bubble collisions, sound waves and turbulence in such a transition produce a GW background peaking near millihertz, in the LISA band.

reason: "Exactly like chiral perturbation theory" overclaims. The method is analogous, and the classical term's coefficient is gauge-dependent.

fix.summary: Power counting in E/M_Pl makes GR a predictive EFT: the Einstein–Hilbert term is leading, and R² terms are suppressed. The leading long-distance quantum correction to the Newtonian potential, (41/10π)Għ/r²c³, is computable and cutoff-independent, in the same way as chiral perturbation theory's non-analytic loop effects.

reason: The double copy yields gravity plus dilaton and B-field. Loop-level colour–kinematics duality is conjectural, so this is not an identity.

fix.summary: Gravity amplitudes are obtained from Yang–Mills amplitudes by replacing colour factors with kinematic numerators that obey the same Jacobi identities (BCJ), generalizing string theory's KLT relations. The classical double copy maps Coulomb to Schwarzschild in Kerr–Schild form.
fix.breaks: The double copy of pure Yang–Mills gives gravity plus dilaton and two-form, not pure GR. The map is proven at tree level (KLT), while colour–kinematics duality at high loop order remains conjectural.

reason: √(2λ) is Maldacena's g²=2πg_s convention. With λ=L⁴/α′² as in C1980 the potential is −4π²√λ/(Γ(1/4)⁴L).
QCD has no known exact string dual, so this is not a duality. Holographic models are applied to QCD.
Diffeomorphism anomalies arise only in the chiral 2D near-horizon effective theory, not generically. Name the Robinson–Wilczek and Christensen–Fulling results.

fix.summary: Regularization breaks classical conformal symmetry, as it breaks axial symmetry in the ABJ anomaly: the trace anomaly sources ⟨T_μ^μ⟩ in curved space and fixes the 2D Hawking flux (Christensen–Fulling 1977). In the chiral 2D near-horizon effective theory, demanding cancellation of the gravitational anomaly also reproduces the Hawking flux (Robinson–Wilczek 2005).

reason: Randall–Sundrum does not lower the fundamental scale; it warps Planck-scale masses down to TeV on the IR brane.

fix.summary: Superstring theory needs six extra dimensions. Large (ADD) extra dimensions lower the fundamental gravity scale to TeV, while warped (Randall–Sundrum) ones redshift Planck-scale masses to TeV on the IR brane. The RS bulk is a slice of AdS5, so hierarchy models and holography share one geometry.

reason: Tachyon-free non-supersymmetric strings exist (SO(16)×SO(16) heterotic). The GSO projection, not worldsheet SUSY alone, gives spacetime SUSY.

fix.name: Superstrings and spacetime supersymmetry
fix.summary: Adding worldsheet fermions gives the RNS superstring. The GSO projection removes the tachyon and yields spacetime supersymmetry in the five 10D superstrings, though tachyon-free non-SUSY strings such as the SO(16)×SO(16) heterotic string exist. Superstring compactifications are the main UV source of SUSY and supergravity model building.

reason: dim G=496 also allows E8×U(1)²⁴⁸ and U(1)⁴⁹⁶, later shown inconsistent. The link is one-sided, so strength 2.

fix.summary: The same consistency principle that fixes SM hypercharges (gauge anomaly cancellation) constrains superstring gauge groups. Gauge and gravitational anomalies of 10D N=1 supergravity cancel via the Green–Schwarz counterterm only if dim G = 496. Of the solutions, SO(32) and E8×E8 are realized; the U(1)-factor options were later shown inconsistent.

reason: Yang–Mills is only the low-energy limit of the DBI action with α′ corrections, so this is a mechanism, not an identity.
The topological expansion matches, but QCD has no known string dual and quarks add boundaries. Mark it as an analogy with breaks.

fix.breaks: No exact string dual of QCD is known. Quark loops add boundaries (open strings) suppressed by N_f/N, and N=3 is not obviously large.

reason: The SME is standard in Lorentz-violation tests but not in core particle-physics curricula, so strength 3 is inflated.
Greenberg's theorem is disputed for nonlocal theories, so the record needs that caveat.

fix.breaks: Greenberg's theorem assumes Wightman-type local QFT. Chaichian, Dolgov, Novikov and Tureanu argue that CPT violation without Lorentz violation is possible in nonlocal theories.

reason: GR contributes only the name and the source tensor; the physics is QCD. The link is one-sided, so strength 1.
Only the Eckart and Landau first-order theories are acausal; the BDNK general-frame first-order theory is causal and stable.

fix.summary: The Eckart and Landau first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics are acausal and unstable (Hiscock–Lindblom). Israel and Stewart's second-order theory, built for relativistic fluids in GR, relaxes the shear tensor over a time τ_π and underlies modern heavy-ion hydrodynamics. Causal first-order (BDNK) frames are a later alternative.

reason: Dynamical ejecta span a broad Y_e range (shock-heated parts are higher), and disk winds can also be neutron-rich. The split is overclaimed.

fix.summary: Which nuclei a merger makes depends on the ejecta electron fraction Y_e. Shock heating, weak interactions and neutrino irradiation set it in NR simulations with neutrino transport. Low-Y_e (≲0.25) ejecta, mainly tidal dynamical with some disk outflows, make lanthanides and the third r-process peak, while higher-Y_e ejecta make lighter elements.

reason: The link to real heavy-ion collisions is a model, not a duality. Chesler–Yaffe show hydrodynamization precedes isotropization.

fix.summary: Colliding gravitational shock waves in AdS5 form a black brane, and the boundary stress tensor hydrodynamizes within about 1/T, before it isotropizes. This models rapid hydrodynamization of the heavy-ion fireball, with horizon formation as its bulk counterpart.

reason: Quadrupole searches apply to Li-7. He/Xe comagnetometers bound dipole b̃ coefficients near 10⁻³³–10⁻³⁴ GeV, while c-coefficients are dimensionless.

fix.summary: Hughes–Drever NMR of Li-7 (J=3/2) searched for quadrupole splitting varying with sidereal orientation. Modern He-3/Xe-129 comagnetometers search for sidereal spin precession. Nuclear-model spin assignments convert the bounds into limits on neutron and proton SME coefficients: b̃ near 10⁻³³–10⁻³⁴ GeV and dimensionless c near 10⁻²⁹.

reason: The universal −γ = −ln D term is defined for 2+1D, where the boundary is a length. The map mixes dimensions.

fix.map: S_{\rm ent}=\alpha\frac{A}{\epsilon^{d-1}}+\dots\ (d\ \text{space dims});\ \ S=\alpha\frac{L}{\epsilon}-\gamma,\ \gamma=\ln\mathcal D\ (2+1\text{D});\ \leftrightarrow\ S_{\rm BH}=\frac{k_BA}{4\ell_P^2}

reason: Only the low-energy Schwarzian sector matches JT gravity. The full bulk dual of SYK is not local gravity, so a breaks clause is needed.

fix.breaks: Only the low-energy Schwarzian sector matches JT gravity. The full SYK bulk dual is stringy and non-local, and SYK's disorder average has no clean bulk counterpart. Lattice SYK models of strange metals are themselves idealizations.

reason: Coating noise is one dominant limit alongside quantum noise, not "the floor". The two-level-system origin is a leading hypothesis, not established.

fix.summary: Around 50–300 Hz, Brownian thermal noise of the amorphous Ta2O5/SiO2 mirror coatings is one of LIGO's dominant limits, alongside quantum noise. Through fluctuation–dissipation (Levin's method) it is set by the coatings' mechanical loss angle, which is attributed to two-level systems in the glass.

reason: The breaks clause contradicts itself: the coupling is O(1) yet called weak. It flows logarithmically to weak coupling.

fix.breaks: Graphene's coupling α_g≈0.5–2.2 flows logarithmically to weak coupling, so it is not a large-N strongly coupled CFT. Disorder and phonons matter, and no gravity dual is known.

reason: Bottom-up models have no known boundary theory, so there is no exact map. This is a method transfer, not a duality.
Bottom-up Hartnoll–Herzog–Horowitz models lack a known microscopic dual, so this is a method transfer, not an exact duality.

record.name: Squeezed vacuum beats the shot-noise limit in LIGO
record.summary: Caves (1981) showed that interferometer shot noise comes from vacuum entering the dark port. Injecting squeezed vacuum lowers shot noise, and frequency-dependent squeezing from filter cavities, used since O4, avoids extra radiation-pressure noise. This is a key quantum-metrology application.
record.map: S_{\rm shot}\to e^{-2r}S_{\rm shot},\ S_{\rm rp}\to e^{2r}S_{\rm rp}\ (\text{fixed quadrature});\ \text{SQL: }S_h^{\rm SQL}=\frac{8\hbar}{m\Omega^2L^2}

record.name: Hayden–Preskill decoding and fast scrambling
record.summary: A black hole past its Page time returns a diary thrown into it after about one scrambling time, t* ~ (β/2π) ln S. Black holes are conjectured to be the fastest scramblers, and the OTOC decay rate saturates λ_L = 2πk_BT/ħ.

record.name: Optical clocks resolve gravitational redshift at millimetre scales
record.summary: Optical lattice clocks, with fractional uncertainty near 10⁻¹⁸, measure the redshift Δν/ν = gh/c² across height differences of centimetres. Bothwell et al. (2022) resolved it within a single millimetre-scale atomic sample. This tests local position invariance and enables relativistic geodesy.
